replies.author: @AHENMOM24
replies.text:
@ImpossibleTravel38​​⁠some seasons are definitely better than others!! I live only about 2 hours straight north of the Island. Hurricane season can get very intense n scary!! 
Like I was a patient on the 8th floor north facing room of Providence Hospital in Mobile on high level bed rest. Being only 2 months postpartum n also 2 months of being treated for SEVERE DVTs (blood clots) in my leg. 
When hurricane Katrina hit!! Everybody who lived through that between Texas n Florida was very nervously watching those final hours pre landfall! 
THEN in full dark of night the night before the WHOLE city of Mobile lost power!! Yea the hospital had the emergency lights in rooms n hallways n in the nurses stations but of course those are extremely dim!! They did move my bed closer to the window but not for long!! Just so I could see what they were all talking about. 
Creepiest scene I’ve ever saw in real life!!

We've all..US ISLANDERS have chosen this beautiful living status and deep down understand with each passing storm..our way of Peaceful life..may be our last. It ALL COMES BACK TWO-FOLD..so we hope, pray, and take each day Slowly In faith, yet with strong Perseverance  for a Safer tomorrow.
